title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
This is page 53 of Grothendieck's sheet numbering; the scan shows '53', and the transcription's '58' is a misreading. The page belongs to the 1986 'fourth version' of Analysis situs. That chapter is an axiomatic attempt at the 'tame topology' announced in Esquisse d'un programme (§5).

The basic object is a 'magma' (M, ≤, ≪̊, |·|):
- M is a poset of 'pieces' (think closed tame subsets).
- X ≪̊ Y is a strict 'interior containment' (X lies in the interior of Y).
- |·| is a further incidence or support structure.
- From these, relations ≪, ≭ and ∥ are derived. The likely meanings are 'well inside', 'meets' or 'non-separated', and 'disjoint'; these readings are inferred, not stated on the page.

An 'atelier' (workshop) associated with M is a set F of 'figures' with an incidence relation ◁ to M. Each figure F has a support F̃ ⊂ M. The relations ≤, ≪, ≭, ∥ on F are transported from M, and Sup and Inf exist.

The page states two things.

(1) Definition-proposition. A subset M' ⊂ M is a sub-magma if:
- (a) M' is a lower set for ≤;
- (b) whenever X ≪̊ Y' ≤ Y with X, Y ∈ M', then Y' ∈ M'. This is a convexity condition on ≪̊-intervals.
Under (a) and (b), M' with the induced ≤, ≪̊, |·| is again a magma. Moreover the derived relations ≪, ≭, ∥ computed inside M' coincide with the restrictions of those computed in M. This was checked axiom by axiom (Mag 1–4) on the previous page. Condition (b) is exactly what makes the derived ≪ of M' equal to ≪ of M restricted to M'.

(2) Definition of restriction. Given an atelier F over M, its restriction to M' is F' = {F ∈ F : F̃ ⊂ M'}, with the induced incidence. This is again an atelier over M'. Its relations ≤, ≪, ≭, ∥ are induced from F. The inclusion F' → F preserves arbitrary Sups and nonempty Infs.

The purpose is to set up the restriction and localisation functoriality of the axiomatics, e.g. passing to an open or closed part. The next page then turns to homomorphisms of ateliers and conditions such as 'stratifiée dirigée', 'quasi-ensembliste' and 'ensembliste' passing to M'.
errors: No genuine error is visible, but the Sup claim is only plausible under the (not stated here) convention that the support of a Sup is the union or ≤-closure of the supports. The Sup of figures supported in M' must have support in M'; this needs M' to be closed under the relevant union operation, which (a) alone does not obviously give. Presumably it follows from the atelier axioms on earlier pages.
Excluding the empty Inf is correct, since the empty Inf is the top element, whose support need not lie in M'.
The second-to-last displayed sentence initially wrote 'associée à F' and corrected it to M'; this is only a slip.

ideas.what: Sub-magma: a ≤-lower subset that is convex for ≪̊-intervals, so that derived relations restrict correctly
ideas.modern_name: substructure or restriction of an abstract stratified or tame-topological structure (analogous to definable subsets in o-minimal structures, or to locally closed unions of strata)
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s); Grothendieck's own axiomatics is unpublished
ideas.where_published: Only the programme is published (Esquisse d'un programme §5–6, on tame topology); the magma and atelier axiomatics is not.

ideas.what: Restriction of an atelier (a set of figures with supports) to a sub-magma; the inclusion preserves arbitrary Sups and nonempty Infs
ideas.modern_name: restriction of a structured lattice of 'figures' to a sub-site; a Sup-preserving embedding of complete lattices

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine bookkeeping in Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatisation of tame topology (magmas and ateliers). The axiomatics itself is little known and unpublished, but this page only checks stability under restriction. That is standard and contains no new idea or connection.
transcription_corrections: Page number at top is '53', not '58' (it follows 52 and precedes 54).
'multigraphe[?]' should read 'magma' throughout, consistent with the previous page ('Soit M un magma, M' une ...', 'est un magma').
'une adhésion[?] associée à M' should read 'un atelier associé à M'; likewise 'c'est bien un atelier associé à M''. The next page speaks of 'ateliers'.
In the first lines, 'On dit que c'est un sous-magma si les 2 [conditions sont satisfaites]' — 'sous-multigraphe' should be 'sous-magma'.
